objective: Yes/no settings given as environment variables are read wrongly: `STOCKROOM_LOW_STOCK_WARNING=false` still turns the low-stock warning on, because any non-empty text counts as true (while the same setting in the INI settings file is read correctly). An environment variable for a yes/no setting must be read exactly as the settings file reads it: `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `1` and `0` in any letter case, with surrounding whitespace ignored; any other text, including empty text, is refused with a `ConfigError`. Environment variables still override the settings file, and other settings are unaffected.
acceptance: The environment values `false`, `False`, `FALSE`, `no`, `No`, `NO`, `off`, `Off`, `OFF` and `0` set `low_stock_warning` to `False`
The environment values `true`, `True`, `TRUE`, `yes`, `Yes`, `YES`, `on`, `On`, `ON` and `1` set `low_stock_warning` to `True`

The environment overrides the settings file in both directions: a file value `yes` with environment `false` gives `False`; a file value `no` with environment `true` gives `True`; without an environment value the file value is used
The environment values `maybe`, `2`, `y`, `t`, `n`, `f`, the empty string, whitespace only, `enabled`, `nope`, `-1`, `truee` and `yes please` are refused with a `ConfigError`
Surrounding whitespace is ignored: ` false `, a tab plus `no` plus a newline, ` Yes` and `1 ` are read as `False`, `False`, `True` and `True`
For every word above, the environment variable gives the same value as the settings file gives for the same word, or both raise a `ConfigError`

Other settings read from the environment (`tax_bp`, `currency_symbol`) are unaffected, unknown variables such as `STOCKROOM_LOW_STOCK` are ignored, and an invalid `STOCKROOM_TAX_BP` is still a `ConfigError`

`stockroom stock` on the sample data prints no warning on stderr when the variable is `false` or `OFF`, prints `warning: 3 item(s) below reorder level` when it is `yes`, and with `sometimes` returns exit code 1, writes `stockroom: error: ...` to stderr and nothing to stdout
